niche: a Dutch and Flemish audiobook subscription app deciding which of its four plans' announced January 2027 price rises go ahead, on each plan's October 2026 base's 2027 contribution under a per-hour publisher remuneration
answer: let Standaard's and Gezin's January 2027 rises go ahead and hold Flex and Onbeperkt (Standaard EUR 2.3 and Gezin 5.4 per October 2026 subscription in 2027; Flex -3.3, Onbeperkt -4.8); two stumps by the factorial, repaired on the holistic audit of 2026-11-13
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst reads the eight past rises by whether they passed the rival, keeps downgraders paying and values each account on its own listening, then carries the October cohort with stopping as final and each account's recent hours, and lets Onbeperkt and Gezin through.
domain_test: Each result is a subscription price-response and LTV quantity (the first bill's extra cancellations and downgrades, the stopped subscriptions' return, the stayers' extra listening, the base still paying and its per-hour remuneration, each plan's change in contribution); reactivation, plan ladders, a rival's price point and per-hour royalties belong to subscription products, and a noun swap into a hospital or factory leaves no such quantities.
layer1: session export rows re-sent by the app after a reconnect
profile ids of removed family profiles absent from today's profile table
playback speed recorded per session, content hours against wall time
app-store subscriptions reported in the stores' own monthly proceeds reports
publisher codes renamed in the 2025 catalogue migration
stakeholder_role: the head of growth, who sets the spring 2027 campaign's lead plan with finance

world.org_type: an audiobook and e-book subscription app

driver: Each option's go or hold rests on what a change does to its existing members over the year, where the members it loses form a pool that comes back at its own rate and at the new terms, and the members who stay use more for months after the change under a cost charged per unit of use, so a fixed group with stopping as final and use held at its recent level, either correction alone, or a pooled response each land on a different wrong set.
driver_concrete: Each plan's January 2027 rise goes ahead only if it raises its October 2026 subscriptions' 2027 contribution at EUR 0.40 per counted hour; the subscriptions a rise loses at the December and first bills partly take a plan up again within the year (light listeners most, before the summer), paying the new price, and those that stay listen more for months after the bill (heavy listeners most), so Standaard goes ahead only with the returns, Onbeperkt holds only with the stayers' extra hours, Flex holds because its 2027 price passes the rival's Basis 10 uur as its 2025 Dutch rise did, and Gezin goes ahead either way.
stump: The platform run's own route (the crossing read with the plan below's profile limit, the December leavers, downgraders kept, each account on its own listening, EUR 0.40 a counted hour) treats a stop as final and the stayers' listening as unchanged and lets Onbeperkt and Gezin through; the returns alone let Standaard, Onbeperkt and Gezin through, the stayers' listening alone Gezin only.
results: R1 paying subscriptions by plan at 31 Oct 2026; R3 extra cancellations per 100 at the first 2027 bill by plan and region; R4 extra downgrades per 100; R9 paying on any plan at 31 Dec 2027 with the rise; R2 the 2027 remuneration per October subscription with the rise; R7 each plan's change in its October base's 2027 contribution; R5 of those that stop by Dec 2027, per 100 paying then; R6 the stayers' extra counted hours over 2027; R8 the rises that go ahead
one_fact_test: the returns sentence rescues R5 and R9 (2 of 9) and not the call; the listening sentence R6 (1 of 9)

differentiation.mark169: mark169 v1 forecast a limit exceeded in one cell of a recurring cycle that one demand component dominates; here a price response is read as a step at an outside reference price across staged rises and valued by who answers under a usage cost, and decides a go-or-hold per plan

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-09: the project lead's review returned the single-deep-step design (one constructed factor, the tutors' stopping hump, placed in the forward cohort by an onboarding pause and surge; every graded figure came out of one projection)
lineage.driver: A unit's chance of reaching a milestone is set largely by whether the provider it is attached to keeps operating, providers stop at a rate that peaks a few months into their own tenure, and the forward group was attached almost wholly to providers in their first months, so an exit curve by the unit's own tenure, which validates on closed groups, overstates how many reach the milestone.
lineage.stump: A competent solver projects the autumn campaign's members on the platform's paid-retention curve by membership month, validated on the spring 2025 campaign and last autumn's joiners, and files about EUR 725 per twelfth-month member, inside the EUR 800 bar, and books the re-run; the step that lands it there is projecting each member on their own tenure when the member's cancellation rides on their tutor, and the autumn members' tutors are about to cross the months in which new tutors stop teaching.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-10: the platform's holistic audit failed the uploaded cut on determinism; repaired (judge DETERMINISTIC APPROVE) but the uploaded run's own methods land the repaired commitment (66.5 of 93 graded weight), the single-total risk: one cut of one total cannot be both forced and hard
lineage.driver: A forward total is the sum of several flows each set by its own mechanism (a step change still applying unit by unit at each unit's anniversary, a one-off shock whose excess exit rate has decayed on a cohort whose exits also run with the calendar, a size adjustment at each anniversary set by how much of its capacity each unit uses on a book whose capacity per user has drifted, a pipeline whose conversion falls with each item's age, and exits that arrive together within groups), so every trailing extrapolation and the recent pooled rates overstate the forward total, and the committed figure is the largest step a filed band, carrying the estimates' own sampling error and nothing else, meets at a stated chance.
lineage.stump: A careful but hurried analyst rebuilds the October 2026 ARR correctly, then applies the mean realised uplift to the contracts still to reprice, pools renewal exit and seat-cut rates without utilisation, first renewals or group exits, carries the Team plan's last three months' exit rates, values the open pipeline at the CRM's stage probabilities and draws accounts independently for the band, and files a commitment above the draft, clearing it, when large contracts negotiate the rise down, seat cuts and exits follow utilisation on a book sold more seats per user each year, the autumn is the Team plan's cancellation peak and the January excess has faded, old open deals rarely close and parent groups leave together, so the commitment sits below the draft; and a ten-minute trailing extrapolation clears the draft by a wide margin because the trailing year carries the price rise and the padded seats as if they recurred.

lineage.driver: Each candidate's value per unit of cost is the payment stream of its future entrants, whose first large drop sits at a price step set by the candidate's own terms and the full price it steps to, whose later decline follows a usage trait the newest entrants carry differently from the record (seen only in a second log at another grain, never in their early survival), which a scheduled price change cuts again at a size read only from an earlier change's whole window and the entrants' tenure at it, and which continues through returns recorded under other identities, so a ranking under a fixed budget on each candidate's own history funds a different set.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each 2027 acquisition line's expected 36-month net revenue per start, set by its 2027 introductory offer and the April 2027 list price at the step-up, the usage its newest starts show in the reading log (social and partner down since late 2025, search up since spring 2025), the April 2027 rise's excess cancellations read from the April 2025 rise including the notice-letter exits and the larger response of first-year subscribers, and later subscriptions by the same household under new customer numbers, ranked per euro of planned spend until the budget is spent.
lineage.stump: A careful but hurried analyst completes each line's newest starts on its older starts' survival, reads the April 2025 jump in end-of-intro exits as a period rather than as the full price, reads the 2025 rise's cancellations from April on pooled over tenure and counts later subscriptions on the customer number, so the four paid social lines and two cashback lines clear 3.5 times their cost and the plan funds 14 lines for EUR 141,575 instead of 8 for EUR 84,308.

lineage.driver: The cost of each option's future entrants is a per-unit charge on a quantity the organisation's own counting engine produces from two reporting channels, one of which the main activity record never sees and which is concentrated in some options, under a rule that counts each item once across both channels, so the activity record scaled to the engine's totals misprices the options in opposite directions and the latest cost per entrant reflects a charging basis that ends.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each plan's first-24-month contribution per spring 2027 trial start is its net revenue over the plan's spring 2024 trial starts' realised months at 2027 prices less EUR 0.40 per counted hour (the 2027 agreement, replacing 2026's 52 per cent of revenue) and the agency's fee, where counted hours are the furthest position each profile first reaches in each title across the live roll-up and the positions downloaded titles report at licence renewal, attributed to the account whose charge listed the profile that month.
lineage.stump: A careful but hurried analyst takes the live roll-up as the listening (it reproduces the 2026 statements exactly) and joins it to today's profile export, which misses Onbeperkt's downloaded listening and credits Gezin with the histories its moved-in profiles brought, and leads with Onbeperkt instead of Gezin; the licence channel alone leads with Standaard.
